media_bytes.description: Size of the published media file, as fetched on accessed_at.

media_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the published media file. A fetch that reproduces this digest reproduces the excerpt; see scripts/fetch_benchmark_media.py.

capture_layout.description: How the speakers were captured, stated only as far as the recording establishes it. single_mixed_track says what a mixdown measurably is - one track, no per-speaker channel to diarize from - and deliberately claims nothing about where the speakers were, since room topology is rarely measurable from a published file. Where the speakers actually were belongs in observations, with its evidence, rather than in an enum a consumer will read alone.

expected_physical_speakers.description: The upper reading of how many people speak: distinct speaking roles heard, before allowing for one person covering two of them. Read it with proven_distinct_speakers, which is the floor; the true count lies between.

proven_distinct_speakers.description: How many speakers are demonstrably different people, by evidence stated in observations. Never larger than expected_physical_speakers. Proving k distinct people needs k speakers established as pairwise distinct from one another: counting the speakers named across a list of pairwise observations overstates it, because a chain of pairs can be satisfied by two people. A diarization score should be read against this floor as well as the estimate.

music_or_effects.description: Whether music or effects appear in the recording. null means not assessed - a candidate ruled out on rights before anyone listened has nothing to report here, and false would claim an observation that was never made.

method.description: How the truth was established, including which provider produced any machine-assisted output. Required once any target is verified, so a score is never read without its annotation provenance.

contaminating_providers.description: Providers that helped build this truth and therefore cannot be scored against it without declaring the dependency. Machine-readable so a scoring run can refuse the combination instead of relying on someone having read the notes. Required once any target is machine-assisted.

license_url.description: URL of the license document, or null when the source is all-rights-reserved and no license document exists.

kind.description: person is a physical speaker at the table; character is the fiction they voice. The two are deliberately separate kinds.

anchor_ms.description: Where the target is observable, in milliseconds on the same basis as the excerpt window. Must fall inside that window.

basis.description: How the target was found. audio_observed is a human ear on the recording. audio_machine_assisted is the recording read through tooling, which is verifiable but carries a dependency on whatever produced the reading. metadata_inferred came from a title, description, or index, and cannot be scored as capability. Only the first two can be verified; the distinction between them is kept in the enum so a consumer reading the field alone cannot mistake one for the other.
